title: Hollow Knight meets Binding of Isaac, with real physics — 32 working days with Claude Code and zero Unity experience. Devlog + process, feedback welcome
author: BrilliantBorder3844
selftext:
**The pitch:** you play a 2D character made of real physics, exploring procedural metroidvania maps. Every chest  
you open changes the *mechanics*, not just the numbers — so every run plays differently. Hollow Knight's  
exploration, Isaac's run-changing items, and a body that tumbles, rolls and gets thrown.  
**Me:** iOS developer, part-time, **zero Unity experience** when this started. Claude Code writes almost all of  
the code; I design, play every build and decide.  
**Before any code (2 days)**  
Researched competitors (Dead Cells, Hades, Hollow Knight, Isaac, Spelunky, Rogue Legacy…).  
Distilled 10 game design books and online material into checklists, then into 3 Claude skills: validate an  
idea, audit a design doc, teach me.  
Built a playable web proof of concept with ChatGPT in an afternoon. It was good enough that I decided to do it  
for real.  
**Day by day (only days with commits)**  
**Week 1: from nothing to a full run**  
**Day 1:** design bible, decision log and an AI pipeline (GitHub issue → Claude → PR, running overnight).  
**Day 2:** Unity project. A square with real physics, plain shapes on plain platforms. 3 classes, first combat.  
**Day 3:** first enemies, first boss, cards, rooms written as text files.  
**Day 4:** a full run is playable. The game records its own runs on video.  
**Day 5:** analysis of 23 competitors against our physics body; first enemy art.  
**Day 6:** knock enemies into each other ("bowling"); first playtest build; the test suite went from 136 s to 23 s.  
**Week 2: it starts looking like a game**  
**Days 7–8:** the enemies get faces and poses; the physics body matches the drawn size.  
**Day 9:** procedural map in-game, wooden UI kit, two rounds of outside critique.  
**Day 10:** the whole forest art pass in one day (105 commits).  
**Days 11–13:** real tilemaps, connected rooms, parallax, and a bot that plays the game through a file bridge.  
**Weeks 3–4: the map**  
**Days 14–15:** 98 room templates, routes and dead ends that pay off. Before this, a few days with no commits  
went into porting the physics of an earlier game of mine to compare side by side.  
**Days 16–19:** telemetry per room, backlog moved to GitHub, −219 MB of GPU memory, permanent movement unlocks.  
**Pause.** September went mostly to design: re-reading, cutting, deciding. Days 20–21 are two short sessions in  
there.  
**October: the vertical slice**  
**Day 22:** play, record, fix. Runs now end at death or at the boss.  
**Day 23:** 3 waves of cards; dead enemies become bowling balls.  
**Day 24:** ChatGPT concept art, then rebuilding the menu in Unity until it overlays the concept.  
**Day 25:** challenges that unlock heroes, moves and cards; Windows build; a friend's playtest.  
**Days 26–28:** HUD, the boss, card icons, enemy redesign, new tutorial.  
**Day 29:** cards inspired by the classics: Mario's stomp, Zelda's spin, the star.  
**Day 30:** adaptive music synthesized in code (no audio files); first 11 languages.  
**Day 31:** 19 languages, mirrored Arabic and Hebrew, AI translation review.  
**Day 32:** this trailer, filmed by the game's own tests.  
**The method, briefly**  
**Verifiable or not delegated.** Rules become tests, written before the change. Each new test must be shown  
failing first.  
**Decisions are logged with the why.** \~800 of them. If code and doc disagree, the AI stops and asks.  
**Docs point to the number, they don't copy it.** A test fails when a doc cites a file that no longer exists.  
**Measure, don't guess.** Telemetry, recorded playtests, one subagent per video.  
**Claude drives ChatGPT through the browser** for concept art, icons and translation review.  
**I keep the fun decisions.** The AI proves things are true; it can't tell me if they're good.  
**Numbers:** 764 commits · 1,508 tests · \~800 decisions · 57 research docs · 32 working days in 81 calendar days ·  
1 human.  
**What I'd love feedback on:**  
**The game:** does the pitch read in the video? Which mechanic would make you want to play?  
**The process:** what would you do differently?

comments.author: Valdaraak
comments.body: Maybe it's just me, but I don't see any Hollow Knight *or* Binding of Isaac inspiration here. I see a platformer.

replies.author: BrilliantBorder3844
replies.body:
Fair, the trailer sells the platforming and hides the structure.

HK: rhythmic combat. Every enemy telegraphs its attack, you dodge, then punish in the window after it whiffs. Charms that cost slots, and movement unlocks (dash, double jump, wall jump) that gate routes on the map.

Isaac: procedural rooms that lock until cleared, and chest items that change rules instead of stats (bombs while walking, ricochet arrows, orbiting satellites). They stack, so no two runs play the same.  
The physics is the twist. You tumble, and you can bowl enemies into each other.

You're right that I should show it instead of claiming it, next video will. Thanks, this is the feedback I wanted.
